* An [[International Security Assistance Force]] attack in [[Khost province]] results in the death of 33 militants. [http://ap.google.com/article/ALeqM5i8dGftYb0s4XWdUMRdIVs3vh1CKAD91KSFD80 (AP via Google News)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}
* [[Chrysler]] announces that it will indefinitely close a [[minivan]] plant in [[South St. Louis]], [[Missouri]] and cut production at another due to falling demand for large vehicles. [https://web.archive.org/web/20080705092449/http://ap.google.com/article/ALeqM5if6HTCFwXC90erym0sBymE9FhfaAD91KJE700 (AP via Google News)]
* The [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] upholds a two year ban against [[cycling|cyclist]] [[Floyd Landis]] meaning that he will lose his 2006 [[Tour de France]] title. [https://web.archive.org/web/20080703135559/http://ap.google.com/article/ALeqM5i48aukcOkGntU1MronjNKP31rvjAD91KHI0G0 (AP via Google News)]
* The [[African Union]] meets at [[Sharm el-Sheikh]] in [[Egypt]] with [[Robert Mugabe]] recently reelected as [[President of Zimbabwe]] representing [[Zimbabwe]]. [https://web.archive.org/web/20080701193208/http://allafrica.com/stories/200806300062.html (''The Herald'' via AllAfrica)]
* [[Peru]]'s largest federation of [[mining]] [[trade union|union]]s commences [[strike action]] in order to pressure the [[Congress of Peru]] to pass legislation to improve labor benefits. [http://www.guardian.co.uk/business/feedarticle/7619244 (Reuters via ''The Guardian'')] 
* An [[Ilyushin]] [[Ilyushin Il-76|Il-76]] crashes minutes after takeoff from [[Khartoum International Airport]]. All four [[Russia]]n crew were killed. It is the second major air crash in the country this week. [http://www.jpost.com/servlet/Satellite?cid=1214726157388&pagename=JPost%2FJPArticle%2FShowFull (''Jerusalem Post'')]
* [[MV Princess of the Stars|MV ''Princess of the Stars'']] disaster:
:*The Bureau of Marine Investigation says it has uncovered multiple lapses in Sulpicio's training and orientation of the ship's crew, but cautioned that it cannot yet draw any conclusions about the disaster's cause. [https://web.archive.org/web/20081006162644/http://newsinfo.inquirer.net/breakingnews/nation/view/20080630-145671/BMI-sees-lapses-in-Sulpicios-orientation-of-crew (Inquirer.net)]
:*Sulpicio sue the [[Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration]] and two of its officials for allegedly misforcasting the route of [[Typhoon Fengshen (2008)|Typhoon Fengshen]], which they say makes them responsible for the sinking.
